text: Of what Isaac knows Genesis 22 tells us nothing. He carries the wood; he asks concerning the lamb; and the answer given him is no answer to the question he has asked. The narrator opens no recess of thought or feeling in him, but records only that they went, both of them, together. The phrase returns; its recurrence is made to do the office of explanation. Thus the account brings forward the question of Isaac's consent, and lays it aside unresolved; Obedience, in this reckoning, settles all, and leaves no remainder.
